cases.sentence: Я вперед все расскажу, – и ___ зажегся в ее за минуту пред этим нежных глазах. – «А, вы любите другого и вступили с ним в преступную связь?
cases.explain: «злой свет» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Very well, let us suppose I do that,” she said. “Do you know what the result of that would be? I can tell you it all beforehand,” and a wicked light gleamed in her eyes, that had been so soft a minute before. “ ‘Eh, you love another man, and have entered into criminal intrigues with him?’ ” (Mimicking her husband, she threw an emphasis on the word “criminal,” as Alexey Alexandrovitch did.) “ ‘I warned you of the results in the religious, the civil, and the domestic relation. You have not listened to me. Now I cannot let you disgrace my name—’ ” and my son, she had meant to say, but about her son she could not jest—“ ‘disgrace my name, and’—and more in the same style,” she added. “In general terms, he’ll say in his official manner, and with all distinctness and precision, that he cannot let me go, but will take all measures in his power to prevent scandal. And he will calmly and punctually act in accordance with his words. That’s what will happen. He’s not a man, but a machine, and a spiteful machine when he’s angry,” she added, recalling Alexey Alexandrovitch as she spoke, with all the peculiarities of his figure and manner of speaking, and reckoning against him every defect she could find in him, softening nothing for the great wrong she herself was doing him.

cases.sentence: – Но, Анна, – сказал Вронский убедительным, ___, стараясь успокоить ее, – все-таки необходимо сказать ему, а потом уж руководиться тем, что он предпримет.
cases.explain: «мягким голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “But, Anna,” said Vronsky, in a soft and persuasive voice, trying to soothe her, “we absolutely must, anyway, tell him, and then be guided by the line he takes.”

cases.sentence: – Я знаю, – перебила она его, – как тяжело твоей ___ лгать, и жалею тебя.
cases.explain: «честной натуре» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “I know,” she interrupted him, “how hard it is for your truthful nature to lie, and I grieve for you. I often think that you have ruined your whole life for me.”

cases.sentence: – Я несчастлива? – сказала она, приближаясь к нему и с восторженною улыбкой любви глядя на него, – я – как ___, которому дали есть.
cases.explain: «голодный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I unhappy?” she said, coming closer to him, and looking at him with an ecstatic smile of love. “I am like a hungry man who has been given food. He may be cold, and dressed in rags, and ashamed, but he is not unhappy. I unhappy? No, this is my unhappiness. …”

cases.sentence: Она услыхала голос возвращавшегося сына и, окинув ___ террасу, порывисто встала.
cases.explain: «быстрым взглядом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: She could hear the sound of her son’s voice coming towards them, and glancing swiftly round the terrace, she got up impulsively. Her eyes glowed with the fire he knew so well; with a rapid movement she raised her lovely hands, covered with rings, took his head, looked a long look into his face, and, putting up her face with smiling, parted lips, swiftly kissed his mouth and both eyes, and pushed him away. She would have gone, but he held her back.
